wiki.title: Propel (company)
wiki.text: Propel, Inc. is an American fintech software company that builds services for low income families. It is best known for Providers, a mobile app that allows users to track their Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) balances and other government benefits. Approximately one quarter of American households receiving SNAP benefits are enrolled in the app.

about: Columbus, Ohio, asset manager founded in 2022 by Vivek Ramaswamy and Anson Frericks, offering ETFs and an anti-ESG shareholder engagement approach. In 2025 it merged with Asset Entities and adopted a bitcoin treasury strategy, becoming a listed company (Nasdaq: ASST). Funding shown is about $2.4 billion. Brand is known mainly in investing and political circles. Strive manages ETFs and also runs the Strive bitcoin treasury company, and Vivek Ramaswamy has stepped back from the executive chair.

Griffin Global Asset Management is a company based in Dublin, Ireland, that provides financial services including asset management and commercial finance. Crunchbase shows funding of about 5.4 billion dollars. The nature of its assets, clients and ownership is not clear from the input. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Investcorp is a global alternative asset manager founded in 1982 and headquartered in Manama, Bahrain, with offices in New York, London, Riyadh and Abu Dhabi, managing tens of billions of dollars in private equity, real estate, credit and infrastructure. Clients are institutions and wealthy investors, mainly in the Gulf and internationally. Its shares are listed on the Bahrain Bourse. Known in Gulf finance circles, and with some sports and event sponsorship, but little general consumer brand awareness.

wiki.title: Investcorp
wiki.text: Investcorp is a global alternative investment company headquartered in Manama, Bahrain. Founded in 1982, the firm invests across private equity, real assets, credit, infrastructure, insurance asset management, and other alternative investment strategies. As of July 2026, Investcorp reported $62.3B worth of assets under management.

about: EJF Capital is an Arlington, Virginia alternative asset manager, founded in 2005 by Emanuel Friedman, which specialises in financial services investing, including bank equities, structured credit, and collateralised loan obligations. It manages funds for institutional investors such as pension funds and family offices, with several billion dollars under management. The $1.17 billion figure likely refers to fund capital or raised vehicles. Low public profile outside the finance industry.

It is private equity backed and has grown through acquisitions. Customers are property owners, developers and organisations. Funding shown is about $1.3 billion. B2B with low public brand awareness. about: Brookfield Infrastructure Partners is a Toronto-listed infrastructure investor, with units on the NYSE (BIP) and the Toronto Stock Exchange (BIP.UN), owning utilities, transport, midstream, data infrastructure and cell towers globally. It is a part of Brookfield Asset Management. Revenue in the billions. Crunchbase shows funding of about $1.6 billion. Investor-facing and B2B, with limited consumer brand awareness.

Aukera is a Brussels based investment company active in asset management and energy, according to Crunchbase. It invests in energy-related assets and projects, with funding of about $760 million recorded. The input gives no detail on its specific holdings, clients or ownership. It appears to be a financial investor serving institutional or private capital rather than consumers, so brand visibility is likely very low. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Focus Financial Partners is a St. Louis based partnership of wealth management firms, providing fiduciary advice to high-net-worth families through registered investment advisers across the United States and abroad. It acquired many independent advisory firms and collected fees on client assets under management. It was listed on Nasdaq (FOCS) and was taken private in 2023 by Clayton, Dubilier & Rice and Stone Point Capital in a deal valued around 7 billion dollars. It is B2B and low in public brand awareness.

wiki.title: Focus Financial Partners
wiki.text: Focus Financial Partners Inc. is an American company that invests in independent, fiduciary wealth management firms, being listed on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol FOCS. Headquartered in New York City, it was incorporated in 2004 by Ruediger (Rudy) Adolf, Rajini Kodialam and Leonard (Lenny) Chang.

about: HIG Holdings is described by Crunchbase as a financial services company based in Fort Worth, Texas. Funding shown is about $710 million. Other details are not given, and the name resembles Hilltop-type holdings, so the exact firm is uncertain. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

DigitalBridge is a Boca Raton, Florida investment firm that owns and manages digital infrastructure assets, including data centres, cell towers, fibre networks and small cells, through managed funds (Vantage Data Centers, Switch, DataBank, Landmark). It was formerly Colony Capital and is listed on the NYSE (DBRG), with about 100 billion dollars of assets under management. In 2025 SoftBank agreed to acquire it. Customers are institutional investors. Well known in infrastructure investing, but low consumer brand awareness.

wiki.title: DigitalBridge
wiki.what: American private equity real estate firm
wiki.text: DigitalBridge Group, Inc. is a global digital infrastructure investment firm. The company owns, invests in and operates businesses such as cell towers, data centers, fiber, small cells, and edge infrastructure. Headquartered in Boca Raton, DigitalBridge has offices in Los Angeles, New York, Denver, London, and Singapore. As of June 2025, DigitalBridge had US$106 billion of assets under management.

about: Mirae Asset Securities is the securities arm of Korea's Mirae Asset Financial Group, offering brokerage, investment banking and wealth management, with overseas offices including New York, which is the location in the input. The parent group was founded in 1997 by Park Hyeon-joo. Customers are retail and institutional investors. A well-known financial brand in Korea, with some sponsorship activity. The group has become a global investor, and is known in Korean finance. The US entity is a smaller institutional broker, with little consumer visibility.

about: Finnfund is the Finnish development finance company, based in Helsinki, owned by the Finnish state and other institutions. It invests in companies and projects in developing countries, particularly in Africa, Asia and Latin America, in areas such as renewable energy, financial services, agriculture and forestry. Founded in 1980. It is a development financier with no consumer product brand, so it is a weak F1 sponsorship fit.

Connor, Clark & Lunn Infrastructure is a Toronto-based investment manager that invests in middle-market infrastructure and energy assets, such as power generation, renewables and utilities, in North America and Europe. It is part of Connor, Clark & Lunn Financial Group, a Canadian employee-owned asset manager with hundreds of billions in assets. It serves institutional investors, so has no consumer brand.

about: Mubadala is Abu Dhabi's sovereign investor, wholly owned by the Abu Dhabi government, managing a global portfolio worth hundreds of billions of dollars across aerospace, semiconductors (GlobalFoundries), energy, real estate, healthcare, technology and sport. Its subsidiaries include Mubadala Capital and Mubadala Energy, and it has had a long association with Formula 1 through team shareholdings and sponsorship. Abu Dhabi also hosts a Grand Prix. A strong, existing F1-aligned institution, with high visibility in the Gulf.

about: Inseego is a San Diego company making wireless products for the 5G and 4G market, such as mobile hotspots, MiFi devices, fixed wireless access routers and indoor and outdoor 5G equipment, plus cloud management services for businesses and carriers. Customers are mobile operators such as Verizon and T-Mobile, enterprises, and consumers via carrier channels. Revenue is from hardware sales and subscriptions. Listed on Nasdaq (INSG). Brand recognition mainly with carriers and business buyers, and moderate among mobile hotspot users.

Venture and credit-backed, offering digital loans through partners and its own apps. Customers are underbanked consumers and small businesses. Brand mostly known to fintech investors, with only regional consumer awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Founded around 2017 by Ben Hallock and Robert Clingan. Raised several hundred million dollars of equity and debt capital; the input shows about 1.8 billion dollars of total funding. B2B and investor-facing brand with no consumer visibility.

about: Canadian financial technology company offering consumer investing, trading, crypto, tax filing, chequing and savings accounts and managed portfolios through the Wealthsimple app. Targets mainly younger Canadians, with over 3 million clients and tens of billions of Canadian dollars in assets. Headquartered in Toronto; launched 2014 as part of Power Corporation's group. Private, valued at 10 billion Canadian dollars after a 2025 funding round. Strong Canadian consumer brand with heavy advertising, previous sports and team partnerships.

wiki.title: Wealthsimple
wiki.text: Wealthsimple Inc. is a Canadian online investment management service. The firm was founded in September 2014 by Michael Katchen, Brett Huneycutt, and Rudy Adler and is based in Toronto. As of November 5, 2025, the firm holds over C$170 billion in assets under administration. It is primarily owned by Power Corporation, which holds a 52.4% undiluted stake aggregated through three entities: its wholly-owned subsidiary, its majority-owned subsidiary, and its controlled alternative asset platform.

about: FundPark is a Hong Kong-based fintech providing supply chain and working capital financing to small and medium sized exporters and online sellers in Asia, using data and automation for credit decisions. Located in Kwun Tong, Kowloon; funding shown at about 1.1 billion dollars largely from debt facilities. Customers are SMEs. B2B finance brand with no meaningful consumer awareness. Offers working capital and receivable-backed financing and has been backed by regional funds. Funding shown at around 975 million dollars, including debt facilities. B2B fintech brand, with limited consumer awareness outside the Saudi startup scene. Limited public information - check before outreach.

about: China Galaxy Securities is a major Chinese state-controlled brokerage and investment bank offering securities trading, wealth management, investment banking, asset management and futures services through many branches. Headquartered in Beijing; formed in 2007 from Galaxy Securities. Listed in Hong Kong (6881) and Shanghai (601881), with Central Huijin as its main shareholder. Financial brand with strong awareness among Chinese retail investors, limited global profile.

Rithm Capital is a US asset manager and real estate investor focused on mortgage servicing rights (Newrez), origination, single-family rental, and acquired Sculptor Capital (2023) and Paramount Group. Revenue near 5 billion dollars. Headquartered in New York; formerly New Residential. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (RITM). B2B and investor brand, but its Newrez business serves consumers.

Nakamoto Holdings is a Utah-based company created by David Bailey's Nakamoto bitcoin treasury strategy through a 2025 merger with healthcare company KindlyMD (Murray, Utah), which holds a large bitcoin balance and plans to buy more. Listed on Nasdaq (NAKA). Funding shown is about 965 million dollars. Investor-focused brand, with no wider consumer recognition.

about: Freepoint Commodities is a Stamford, Connecticut commodity merchant that trades and markets physical energy, metals and agricultural products, including crude oil, refined products, natural gas liquids, metals and concentrates. Customers are producers, refiners and industrial buyers worldwide, and it earns trading margins and logistics fees, with offices across Europe, Asia and the Americas. Founded in 2012. Privately held, with funding including a large investment from Hartree Partners and others. B2B trading house with little public consumer awareness.

Alpaca is a San Mateo, California brokerage infrastructure company providing APIs for stock, options and crypto trading, used by fintech apps, banks and developers. Its customers include brokers and apps in the US and Asia, and it earns from payments for order flow, interest and fees. Founded in 2015, it has raised about $763m in total, including a Series D in 2026. Private. Mainly B2B and developer-focused, little consumer awareness.
